newsitem.title: UK: UK retailers welcome EU plans for card payments.
newsitem.headline: UK retailers welcome EU plans for card payments.

text.p: British retailers on Wednesday welcomed European Union proposals to allow shops to charge consumers who use credit and debit cards, even though the UK has allowed this since 1989.
"This would make customers aware of these charges for the first time, extending the benefits enjoyed by UK shoppers to other countries," the British Retail Consortium said.

European banks have long overcharged retailers to process card transactions to cover the cost of issuing cards, the BRC said. And for years, retailers have fought to pass part of the costs charged by the banks onto consumers.
On Monday, the European Commission said it might allow shops to do so. "The Commission has doubts about this rule. It would like it to disappear," a Commission spokesman said.
The BRC said that if the British experience was anything to go by, shoppers will obtain a discount when paying with cash although some operators such as taxis charge a premium for card use instead.

"We are delighted that the competition directorate is giving a signal that they are prepared to tackle the banks and payment schemes," said Elizabeth Staunton Jones, the BRC's financial services director.

The BRC said fees paid to banks by retailers had fallen in the UK since the government abolished the "no discrimination" rule schemes eight years ago. The rule said to allow card users to be charged would discriminate against them.
"This is a first step," Jones said. "Retailers have long argued that the banks overcharge retailers to cover the cost of issuing cards."
The BRC represents about 90 percent of Britain's retail industry.
